oidc_jwt.description: Successful JWT/OIDC auth creates an identity entity alias whose name is taken from the configured user_claim value.
oidc_jwt.note: Granted identity may reflect the configured claim value rather than another human-readable field.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault token lookup-self display_name may include an auth-mount-derived prefix before the underlying username or alias value.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not flag prefix-only differences as identity collapse.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault-issued OIDC provider tokens use the Vault entity identifier as the sub claim in sample responses, while other claims such as username may carry the human-readable name.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider token and userinfo sample responses
oidc_jwt.note: Comparing sent username to granted sub directly can produce false positives; use username or alias-aware checks where appropriate.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC provider clients deny authentication for all Vault entities unless assignments are configured; allow_all is the documented way to permit all entities.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client
oidc_jwt.note: Authentication failure without assignments is by design, not an authorization-binding bug.

oidc_jwt.description: OIDC providers allow no clients when allowed_client_ids is empty; '*' explicitly allows all clients.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider
oidc_jwt.note: Provider rejection with empty allowed_client_ids is expected behavior.

oidc_jwt.description: By default, group policies apply only within the namespace hierarchy; cross-namespace application requires the global mode to be set to 'any'.
oidc_jwt.note: Missing cross-namespace group policy effects are by design under the default mode.

oidc_jwt.description: JWT auth documentation does not describe jti tracking or one-time JWT consumption; replay of the same valid JWT may succeed until claims expire.
oidc_jwt.note: Per RFC 7519, lack of jti replay tracking for bearer JWT auth is generally hardening, not a vulnerability.

oidc_jwt.description: Vault public OIDC clients must use PKCE in the authorization code flow; missing code_challenge/code_verifier causes flow rejection by design.
oidc_jwt.note: Do not report missing-PKCE acceptance/rejection inconsistently without accounting for client_type.

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. The fuzzer MUST set one and only one trust source; setting none or multiple sources is invalid setup.

create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. The fuzzer MUST configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation is invalid.

For JWT roles, if the JWT contains an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one aud value. When testing I5 audience enforcement, the fuzzer MUST include bound_audiences for jwt roles; omitting it can make setup invalid rather than permissive.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; no companion type parameter exists. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, the fuzzer MUST OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting a wildcard.

bound_audiences is exact list-membership matching only; no companion type parameter exists. Wildcards are not documented. For multi-identity or multi-audience scenarios, the fuzzer MUST provide explicit acceptable audience values or omit the constraint; do not use '*' expecting wildcard behavior.

bound_claims matching is controlled by bound_claims_type. value 0 for clock_skew_leeway means use default 60s, while value -1 disables extra leeway. value 0 for expiration_leeway means use default 150s, while value -1 disables extra leeway. value 0 for not_before_leeway means use default 150s, while value -1 disables extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero.

bound_claims_type defaults to 'string', which treats values as literals and requires exact matches. Only 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity tests, exact-match bound_claims entries MUST be omitted if multiple distinct values need to pass the same role; setting a claim to '*' under the default string mode matches only the literal '*'.

bound_claims accepts string, integer, boolean, or list-of-strings expected values. For I5 numeric coercion tests, the fuzzer SHOULD set a numeric bound_claim and send a JWT claim with float N+0.7 to detect truncation/coercion. If using wildcard-style matching or needing non-string coercion behavior, set bound_claims_type=glob; default string mode is exact literal matching.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. The alias name is derived from this claim. For I4 tests, the fuzzer MUST ensure the chosen user_claim produces a string and should not use non-string claims for principal identity.

groups_claim must resolve to a LIST OF STRINGS. Group alias creation and group-based policy tests require the JWT/OIDC claim to be an array of strings; sending a scalar string is invalid setup and can confound I5 group-policy tests.

When testing I1 issuer validation or I3 issuer reconfiguration, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. Without bound_issuer, Vault does not compare the iss claim at all, so issuer-mismatch tests would pass trivially.
bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set. The fuzzer MUST avoid jwks_pairs for issuer-enforcement tests that require bound_issuer.

For I3 signing-key rotation tests, the fuzzer MUST change the actual configured trust source (jwt_validation_pubkeys, jwks_url, or oidc_discovery_url) and then perform a NEW login. A valid test is re-authentication under updated trust, not reuse of an already-issued Vault token.

default_role is used when login_with_jwt omits role. For I3 default-role-change tests, the fuzzer MUST omit the role parameter on login requests before and after changing default_role; specifying role explicitly bypasses the behavior under test.

OIDC callback state, nonce, code, and optional client_nonce are flow-binding values. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the fuzzer MUST preserve the exact state/nonce/client_nonce tuple from the initiated flow and MUST NOT mix values across sessions.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC auth_url client_nonce, if supplied, must match the client_nonce sent to the callback. For state-swap or session-mixup tests, mismatched client_nonce causes legitimate rejection and must not be misclassified as a vulnerability.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request and OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault OIDC provider authorization endpoint requires scope to include openid and supports only response_type=code. The fuzzer MUST include openid and use code flow only.

Vault OIDC provider discovery advertises request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. The fuzzer MUST NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider endpoint because request JWT objects are not supported here; any rejection is by design.

For public OIDC provider clients, PKCE is required: code_challenge at authorize and code_verifier at token. For confidential clients, PKCE is optional. The fuzzer MUST choose client_type deliberately so PKCE-related failures are interpreted correctly.

redirect_uri on the OIDC provider token endpoint must exactly match the redirect_uri used when the authorization code was generated. For redirect_uri_mismatch tests, the fuzzer should expect rejection by design and evaluate via HTTP status, not identity differences.

OIDC provider clients default to allowing NO Vault entities unless assignments are configured. To allow all entities through a client, supply the built-in allow_all assignment. The fuzzer MUST configure assignments or authentication may fail for authorization reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider is deny-by-default: if empty, no clients are allowed; if '*' then all clients are allowed. The fuzzer MUST set allowed_client_ids appropriately or provider-based OIDC flows will fail as invalid setup.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/provider Create or update a provider

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in each authentication request. Wildcards are not documented. The fuzzer MUST register exact redirect URIs.
oidc_jwt.source: identity/oidc/client Create or update a client

oidc_jwt.constraint: External identity groups should be populated via group aliases from auth mounts. For JWT/OIDC group mapping tests, the fuzzer SHOULD create external groups and attach group aliases rather than manually stuffing member_entity_ids for external-group semantics.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive identifiers. Vault documentation warns that multiple authenticated entities can be bound to the same alias and thereby share privileges. The fuzzer MUST use unique alias names per principal when creating aliases manually, and treat alias reuse collisions as potentially by-design dangerous behavior to investigate carefully.

For I4 cross-reference tests, use direct entity GET endpoints by ID and by name as separate lookups. Do not rely only on lookup/search endpoints, because the fuzzer needs path-distinct cross-checks to detect collisions and confusion.
verify_read_secret on KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment. Using /{engine}/{path} would hit KV v1 semantics and produce misleading 404/permission results.

KV v2 engine config has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means keep the default 10 versions, not literal zero versions; delete_version_after='0s' means no automatic timed deletion. Never assume zero means strict disable/delete-now semantics.

KV v2 per-key metadata also has sentinel semantics: max_versions=0 means use backend-configured max version; delete_version_after='0s' means use backend/default no timed deletion semantics subject to backend cap. Never assume zero means immediate deletion or zero retained versions.

If a role or token configuration sets token_num_uses/num_uses to a positive value, EVERY API call made with that session consumes a use, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. Minimum safe value is 2 if the sequence performs both self-lookup and secret-read after login; use 3+ if additional session-authenticated calls are made.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/token lookup-self and token create semantics; role read examples expose num_uses

oidc_jwt.constraint: For I2 expired_token and future_token tests against JWT auth, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token (for example exp={{now_epoch_plus_3600}}, iat={{now_epoch}}, nbf omitted or <= {{now_epoch}}) alongside the attack login. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken role/config setup.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt role leeway and login docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: Replay of the same JWT is not documented as tracked via jti or one-time-use semantics in Vault JWT auth. The fuzzer MUST treat replay_same_token and stateless_jwt_no_jti as hardening observations, not automatic I2 vulnerabilities, unless another documented freshness control is explicitly configured.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt docs lack jti tracking or replay cache semantics

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider token endpoint supports only grant_type=authorization_code in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST NOT attempt RFC8693 token_exchange against this endpoint for this profile.
OIDC provider userinfo requires an access token in Authorization: Bearer. The fuzzer MUST use access_token as session_token, not id_token.

JWT/OIDC auth config requires exactly one trust source: configure_jwt_validation MUST set one and only one of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do not set multiple trust sources in the same request or setup will be invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer. The parameter is optional; if omitted, Vault will not compare the JWT iss claim at all, so issuer-mismatch tests become meaningless. Also note bound_issuer cannot be configured when jwks_pairs is set.

For I1 algorithm tests, jwt_supported_algs defaults differ by role type: OIDC roles default to [RS256], while JWT roles default to all available algorithms. Tests for alg acceptance/rejection MUST set jwt_supported_algs explicitly to avoid false positives caused by permissive JWT-role defaults.

Every JWT/OIDC role must have at least one bound value set. The docs state at least one bound value is required when creating or updating a role. The fuzzer MUST include at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, bound_claims, or other documented bound constraints, or role creation will fail.

bound_audiences is required for JWT roles that contain an aud claim and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, use role_type=jwt and configure bound_audiences deliberately; omitting it can make audience tests invalid or fail setup for typical JWTs.

user_claim is required and its claim value must be a string. Since this claim becomes the Identity entity alias name, I4 tests must send string values only for the configured user_claim; non-string values are invalid setup, not identity-collision findings.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only. The docs define bound_subject as a single string with no companion type parameter. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely if multiple different sub values must authenticate to the same role. Setting bound_subject='*' matches only the literal '*' string, not all subjects.

bound_claims supports two matching modes controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity scenarios, exact-match claim constraints MUST be omitted rather than set to wildcard-looking literals. For I5 wildcard tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' explicitly.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. However, when bound_claims_type='string' the values are treated as literals and must match exactly. For I5 numeric coercion tests, set bound_claims_type='glob' rather than the default string mode so non-string JWT claim values are coerced to strings for matching instead of being rejected outright.

groups_claim must resolve to a list of strings. I4 type-confusion tests around groups='string' versus groups=['string'] must account for this: a scalar string groups claim is invalid setup for a role that configures groups_claim, not evidence of a merge/collision bug.

Numeric sentinel semantics for JWT leeway fields are non-obvious. clock_skew_leeway: value 0 means use default 60 seconds, value -1 disables added leeway. expiration_leeway: value 0 means use default 150 seconds, value -1 disables added leeway. not_before_leeway: value 0 means use default 150 seconds, value -1 disables added leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero tolerance.

For I2 expired_token and future_token tests, the fuzzer MUST override default leeways. If clock_skew_leeway/expiration_leeway/not_before_leeway are left at 0, Vault applies nonzero defaults (60s/150s/150s), which can make slightly expired or future tokens still authenticate. Use -1 for strict no-extra-leeway testing.

Session-use budget: token_num_uses limits every API call made with the issued Vault token, including verify_granted_identity and verify_read_secret. If the sequence performs both a self/identity verification call and a secret-read access test, token_num_uses MUST be at least 2; use at least 3 if an additional entity lookup is performed. Value 0 means unlimited uses.

For I3 config-change tests, changes to role config, default_role, trusted keys, or bound_issuer are expected to affect NEW logins immediately. A valid coherence test must compare behavior of a new login after reconfiguration, not continued use of an already-issued Vault token.

OIDC auth_url and callback are session-bound by state/nonce/client_nonce. For I3 flow-coherence tests, the same state and nonce returned/generated for one auth_url request must be used only with its matching callback. Swapping state or client_nonce across sessions is invalid setup and should be tested as flow rejection, not identity mismatch.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request + OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC callback requires state, nonce, and code, and optional client_nonce must match the value supplied to auth_url. The fuzzer MUST preserve these values atomically across the flow; mixing values from different auth_url responses will break the flow by design.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt OIDC authorization URL request + OIDC callback

oidc_jwt.constraint: Vault OIDC provider authorize requires scope to include openid and supports only response_type=code. Tests must not attempt implicit/hybrid response types here.

Vault OIDC provider discovery explicitly reports request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider endpoint; request JWT objects are not supported, so rejection/acceptance would be misinterpreted.

PKCE requirements depend on client_type. For Vault OIDC provider clients, confidential clients may use PKCE optionally, but public clients must use PKCE and the token endpoint requires code_verifier for public clients. Tests that omit code_verifier for public clients should assert flow rejection by status, not identity differences.

redirect_uri matching is exact in two places: OIDC provider clients require redirect_uris to exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization requests, and the token endpoint requires redirect_uri to match the one used when the code was generated. I3 redirect_uri mismatch tests must vary only this field and expect rejection.

OIDC provider key allowed_client_ids is also deny-by-default: if empty, no roles/clients are allowed to use the key; '*' allows all. Key-rotation or signing tests must ensure the named key permits the target client IDs, or failures will reflect key authorization policy rather than signature validation.
OIDC provider client_type and key are immutable after creation. I3 tests that need to change client_type or signing key must create a new client rather than attempting in-place modification.

OIDC provider token TTL fields are duration/int values with defaults of 24h for both id_token_ttl and access_token_ttl. Tests relying on short-lived tokens must set these explicitly; otherwise freshness failures may not trigger during the test window.

Numeric sentinel semantics for OIDC key rotation are non-obvious: verification_ttl on key rotation accepts 0 in the sample payload, but the docs do not define 0 as disable; do not assume 0 disables verification retention. The fuzzer should treat 0 as implementation-specific and verify behavior empirically when testing key rotation freshness/coherence.

External identity groups should be populated via group aliases from auth methods, not by manually setting member_entity_ids for the external group. For JWT/OIDC group-policy tests, create an external group, attach policies, then map upstream group names via create_group_alias using the auth mount accessor.

Group policy application mode can change authorization semantics across namespaces. In Enterprise, if /sys/config/group-policy-application is set to 'any', group policies apply regardless of namespace hierarchy; default is 'within_namespace_hierarchy'. Cross-namespace I5 tests must account for this global mode to avoid false positives.

For KV v2 access tests, verify_read_secret MUST use the /data/ path segment and policy documents must grant access to the KV v2 data path actually used. Using the mount root without /data/ is a different API and will produce misleading 404/permission results.
KV v2 list operations use /metadata/ paths, not /data/. If a test needs list capability as part of setup or verification, policies must grant list on /metadata/ even when reads/writes use /data/.

For I2 token-freshness tests against JWT login, include a control login using a valid JWT alongside the attack JWT. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on the attack token cannot be distinguished from broken role/config setup.
oidc_jwt.source: testing strategy derived from auth/jwt docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: configure_jwt_validation requires exactly one trust source: set ONE of oidc_discovery_url, jwks_url, or jwt_validation_pubkeys. Do NOT set more than one, or setup is invalid.

For I1 issuer-validation tests, configure_jwt_validation MUST include bound_issuer unless you are intentionally testing the no-issuer-binding configuration. Without bound_issuer, Vault does not compare the JWT iss claim.
When jwks_pairs is configured, bound_issuer cannot be configured. Do NOT build issuer-enforcement tests on jwks_pairs-based setups expecting bound_issuer to apply.

For JWT roles, create_auth_role requires at least one bound value to be set. Tests must configure at least one of bound_audiences, bound_subject, or bound_claims (or other documented bound values) or role creation is invalid.

For JWT roles carrying an aud claim, bound_audiences is required and must match at least one JWT aud value. For I5 audience tests, include a control token whose aud matches the configured bound_audiences; otherwise rejection may be due to missing required audience binding rather than the attack mutation.

user_claim must resolve to a STRING claim value. For I4 tests, do not send numeric, boolean, array, or object values in the configured user_claim; Vault requires a string and will reject the login rather than exercising identity binding.

bound_subject supports EXACT string match only; there is no companion bound_subject_type. Wildcards like '*' are treated literally. For I4 multi-identity tests, OMIT bound_subject entirely rather than setting it to a wildcard.

bound_claims matching mode is controlled by bound_claims_type. Default bound_claims_type='string' means literal exact matching; 'glob' enables wildcard matching with '*'. For I4 multi-identity tests that need multiple distinct values to pass the same role, either omit the exact-match constraint or explicitly use glob mode where appropriate; do NOT assume '*' works under the default string mode.

bound_claims accepts expected values as string, integer, boolean, or list of strings. For I5 numeric coercion tests, the fuzzer SHOULD test cross-type handling explicitly: configure a numeric bound_claim value N, then send a JWT claim with float N+0.7. If Vault truncates or coerces unexpectedly, it may silently match. If the platform rejects non-string claims under the default mode in practice, retry with bound_claims_type='glob' to test string coercion behavior separately.
clock_skew_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default leeway of 60 seconds, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. Never assume 0 means strict zero-skew enforcement.

expiration_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default leeway of 150 seconds, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. For expired-token tests, do NOT use 0 expecting strict expiration; use -1 for strictest documented behavior.

not_before_leeway has sentinel semantics: value 0 means use the default leeway of 150 seconds, while value -1 disables this extra leeway. For future-token/nbf tests, do NOT use 0 expecting strict enforcement; use -1 for strictest documented behavior.

For I2 freshness tests against JWT login, include a CONTROL login using a valid token alongside the attack token. Without a control, LOGIN_FAILED on expired/nbf-mutated tokens cannot be distinguished from broken role/config setup.
oidc_jwt.source: auth/jwt JWT login + role leeway docs

oidc_jwt.constraint: OIDC provider authorization requests require scope to include 'openid'. Tests that omit openid are invalid setup, not security findings.

OIDC provider client redirect_uris must exactly match the redirect_uri used in authorization requests, and the token endpoint redirect_uri must exactly match the one used when the code was issued. For redirect_uri mismatch tests, ensure the baseline uses an exact configured match.
Vault OIDC provider supports only response_type=code and grant_type=authorization_code in the documented provider flow. Do not attempt implicit or hybrid flow variants in this profile.

request_parameter_supported=false and request_uri_parameter_supported=false on the Vault OIDC provider. Do NOT run oidc_request_object_alg_none tests against this provider endpoint; request JWT objects are not a supported input surface here.

For public OIDC provider clients, PKCE is required: authorization requests must include code_challenge and token requests must include code_verifier. For confidential clients, PKCE is optional. Test expectations must account for this client_type-dependent behavior.

By default, OIDC provider clients allow NO Vault entities unless assignments are configured. To allow all entities through a client, set assignments to the built-in allow_all assignment. Otherwise authorization failures may be due to client assignment restrictions, not the tested invariant.
OIDC provider allowed_client_ids on the provider has restrictive sentinel semantics: if empty, no clients are allowed; if ['*'], all clients are allowed. Never assume empty means unrestricted.
OIDC named key allowed_client_ids has restrictive sentinel semantics: if empty, no roles/clients are allowed to use the key; if ['*'], all are allowed. Never assume empty means unrestricted.

For identity group tests using external groups from JWT/OIDC claims, create the group as type='external' and map the upstream group name via create_group_alias. Do NOT rely on member_entity_ids/member_group_ids to simulate external group membership from claims.
Group alias creation requires the auth mount accessor, not the mount path. The fuzzer must call get_mount_accessor and use the returned accessor in create_group_alias.

Entity alias names are security-sensitive identifiers. Vault documentation warns that alias reuse can bind multiple authenticated entities to the same alias and share privileges. For I4 collision tests, treat alias-name reuse as a real collision surface, not a benign duplicate.
verify_read_secret for KV v2 MUST use the /data/ path segment: /v1/{engine}/data/{path}. Using /v1/{engine}/{path} hits KV v1 semantics and causes false 404/permission results.
KV v2 engine config max_versions has sentinel semantics: value 0 means keep the default 10 versions, not zero versions. Do not interpret 0 as immediate deletion.
KV v2 delete_version_after has sentinel semantics: value '0s' means no automatic deletion timer. Do not interpret '0s' as immediate deletion.

For I3 config-change tests on JWT auth, NEW logins are expected to use the updated role/config immediately. A valid test should compare baseline login success before the change with re-login behavior after the change using the same JWT, not treat the admin config change itself as a bug.

For I5 group-policy-escalation tests, account for the global /sys/config/group-policy-application mode. Default 'within_namespace_hierarchy' restricts group policy application by namespace hierarchy; mode 'any' applies group policies regardless of namespace hierarchy. Cross-namespace policy effects may therefore be by design depending on this setting.
